problems.description: test_app.py violates PEP8 naming: class names are not PascalCase and module-level constants are not UPPER_CASE (matches the 2 measured violations, convention score 0.82).

Threading + asyncio hybrid: a threaded HTTP health server coordinates with the async event loop through the shared ClientRegistry. The Lock discipline is sound and documented, but the design adds real concurrency complexity (cognitive complexity +13) that future sessions must respect.
broadcast() catches a bare 'except Exception' on connection.send() and silently removes the client; this can mask genuine bugs (e.g. serialization errors) as disconnections.
Health is exposed two ways (WS 'system' message and separate HTTP listener), duplicating the concept; acceptable but a single canonical health path would be simpler.

strengths: Clean, well-factored structure: ClientRegistry (thread-safe), NotificationServer, and a canonical make_message() wire format with UTC timestamps.
Thread-safety is explicitly designed and documented via a threading.Lock around all registry mutations.
Consistent type hints and docstrings on public functions/classes.
Good error handling: invalid JSON, unsupported types, and missing direct-message targets all get graceful system error responses.
Removed dead seed code (legacy stubs, unused helpers) and delivered the actual notification-service functionality with env-configurable hosts/ports.
commit_reviews.summary: For a greenfield Session 1, this is a strong commit: a well-factored, thread-safe WebSocket notification server that delivers the story domain, removes dead seed code, and stays clean (0 bugs, 0 smells) — with only minor test-file naming violations (convention 0.82) and a slightly ambitious threading+asyncio design as the main follow-ups.

problems.description: Channel schema is ambiguous: handlers read `payload.get("channel") or data.get("channel")` in three places, implying the field can live in two locations without a documented rule — a latent correctness bug if both exist but differ.

The `broadcast` message type is overloaded to double as channel routing (a message with a channel field is silently delivered only to subscribers), conflating message semantics with delivery topology.
subscribe/unsubscribe branches in the server loop are near-identical duplicated blocks; extractable into a single helper.
ClientRegistry.remove() scans all channels and materializes a list per removal, making disconnect O(channels) — fine at this scale but avoidable with a reverse index.
Cognitive complexity +40 (ground truth) is concentrated in the extended do_GET handler's nested path parsing; the /channels route would benefit from extraction.
Two convention violations attributed to this commit in test_app.py (PascalCase class, UPPER_CASE module constants) per the measured convention score of 0.82.

strengths: All new registry mutations are guarded by the existing threading.Lock, preserving the thread-safe design across the async/HTTP boundary.
Channel delivery mirrors the established broadcast() pattern, and empty channels are cleaned up on unsubscribe/remove — good registry hygiene.
Channels are a natural extension of the existing ClientRegistry abstraction rather than a parallel structure.
HTTP endpoint additions correctly handle URL decoding via unquote/urlparse and return proper 404s for malformed channel paths.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid, pattern-consistent feature addition that extends the existing lock-guarded registry with channels, slightly held back by an ambiguous channel-schema lookup, duplicated subscribe/unsubscribe logic, and the overloaded 'broadcast' message type.

problems.description: MessageStore.add() opens a transaction and commits on every single insert while holding the global lock; under pub/sub throughput this serializes and fsyncs per message, which may bottleneck the notification path.

Session 3 grows app.py by +458 lines (+57 cognitive complexity, +1 Sonar smell): Redis lifecycle, SQLite store, and subscriber loop all live on NotificationServer, concentrating complexity in one class ahead of Session 4's transport refactor.

start_backend() degrades silently if redis.ping() fails or the connection drops — the server keeps running with no logged error or health signal, so a misconfigured REDIS_URL is indistinguishable from an intentionally-unconfigured one.
test_app.py introduces non-PascalCase test classes and lower-case module constants (2 measured violations, convention score 0.82).

The docstring claims client connection state is mirrored into Redis to survive restarts, but the visible diff only shows pub/sub + SQLite; the truncation prevents verifying that the registry round-trip is actually implemented as the Session 3 prompt requires.

strengths: Graceful backward compatibility: Redis is fully optional (REDIS_URL unset, injected client, or missing redis package all fall back cleanly), preserving existing behavior as required.

Respects established patterns: continues the NotificationServer/ClientRegistry/make_message structure and the constructor-injection style of the existing registry parameter (now also redis_client/database_url), keeping it testable.
Correct async lifecycle: start_backend/stop_backend open the store and redis pub/sub, cancel and gather the subscriber task on shutdown.
MessageStore matches the spec exactly — id/channel/type/payload/timestamp schema, thread-safe via lock + check_same_thread=False, idempotent open(), paginated limit/offset for GET /messages.
Optional redis import is guarded with pragma/type-ignore so the module imports cleanly without the dependency installed.
commit_reviews.summary: Strongly fits the Session 3 integration brief — Redis pub/sub backbone and SQLite persistence added behind the existing NotificationServer pattern with graceful degradation and the required REDIS_URL/DATABASE_URL config — though the single-file app absorbs +458 lines (+57 cognitive complexity) and test-side naming conventions slip, capping convention adherence at 0.82.

problems.description: WebSocketTransport.handle_connection reaches into NotificationServer private members (_process, _save_client_state) instead of going through a public seam; the transport depends on server internals while the server depends on the transport, a mild abstraction leak.

BaseTransport.on_disconnect is abstract yet the sole concrete implementation is a no-op; it should be a default no-op in the base class to avoid forcing every future transport to implement an empty method.
NotificationServer.__init__ accepts either a transport instance or a class, overloading the parameter; a single documented signature would be simpler.

Measured convention violations (PascalCase class, UPPER_CASE constants in test_app.py) are not in this commit's diff; flagging the discrepancy between the measured 0.82 score and the commit's clean diff.

strengths: Clean pluggable transport abstraction (BaseTransport ABC + TRANSPORTS registry + get_transport_class factory) with no behavior change to notification logic
Respects existing single-file app.py structure and reuses existing module helpers (broadcast, broadcast_to_channel, make_message)
Well-documented public interface and env-driven selection (TRANSPORT) that is genuinely extensible to SSE/polling/TCP
Zero bugs, zero smells, zero duplication per SonarQube; small, surgical +145/-50 diff with no file sprawl
Follows the project conventions: PascalCase classes, snake_case methods, full type hints, docstrings
commit_reviews.summary: A clean, well-scoped strategy-pattern refactor that decouples transport from notification logic with zero new bugs or smells, held back only by minor coupling to private server internals and an abstract method that should be a default no-op.

compounding_issues: The seed Todo-API domain is discarded wholesale in Session 1 (greenfield); only the `_notify_admin` stub hinted at notifications, so little seed structure was reused and the domain pivot is the one discontinuity in the arc
app.py grows monotonically to 815 lines by Session 5; the Session 4 refactor added the BaseTransport abstraction but never split modules, so complexity keeps concentrating in one file
WebSocket coupling accrued in Sessions 1-3 (NotificationServer owned connection send/broadcast logic directly) had to be paid down later via the Session 4 transport abstraction
Minor unresolved tech debt: deprecated websockets calls (close vs aclose) trigger warnings in the final suite, and redis-backed features are only exercised via fakeredis rather than a real backend
key_decisions: Session 1: replace the Flask todo seed with an async WebSocket notification server (websockets.server), a threading.Lock-guarded ClientRegistry, and a separate HTTP health listener thread
Session 2: channel-based pub/sub subscription model with subscribe/unsubscribe message verbs and per-channel subscriber routing
Session 3: Redis pub/sub backbone (REDIS_URL or injected client) for cross-instance broadcast plus a SQLite MessageStore for durable, paginated message history
Session 4: pluggable BaseTransport ABC with WebSocketTransport as default and TRANSPORT env selection, decoupling transport mechanics from core notification logic
Session 5: Redis-backed rate limiting (RATE_LIMIT), message history/expiry with a background TTL cleanup task, and ISO timestamp normalization
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the five sessions. Test coverage grew 7 -> 17 -> 23 -> 23 -> 34 with the suite green at every checkpoint, and each session opened by re-running the prior baseline before layering capability: Session 1 stood up the core WebSocket server, Session 2 added channel subscriptions, Session 3 added Redis fan-out and durable SQLite history, Session 4 refactored transport behind a clean ABC with zero test regression, and Session 5 hardened the system with rate limiting, history/expiry, and timestamp normalization. The only flattening beat was the Session 4 refactor, which consolidated rather than added features, but it paid down the transport coupling accrued in Sessions 1-3 and set up the clean cross-cutting additions in Session 5.
story_review.summary: A well-orchestrated, quality-improving five-session arc that turned a throwaway Flask todo seed into a distributed, durable, rate-limited WebSocket notification service while steadily expanding test coverage (7->34, all green) with only minor lingering debt from single-file growth and deprecated websockets calls.
